key_highlights: ASX slumped as bond yields spiked; unemployment hit 5-year high, yet RBA signals further rate hikes — stagflation risk elevated
AUD 'pulverised' by US economic boom; AUD/USD under severe pressure
Trump diesel export ban flagged as 'Australian nightmare' for energy security and fuel costs
Intergenerational Report 2026 underscores urgent need for tax reform amid fiscal pressure
Property market cooling: rising listings, falling demand pushing prices lower
Mining exploration active: Rio2 Peruvian copper drill, Sarytogan 452m copper intercept, multiple gold discoveries (Auric, Forrestania, Manhattan)
Jetstar industrial action escalates; staff waiving fees — consumer sector pressure
More than half of Australian renters financially struggling — consumer stress deepening

sectors.trend: Exploration momentum strong across copper (Rio2, Sarytogan), gold (Auric, Forrestania, Manhattan), and rare earths (Lindian). However, macro headwinds from AUD weakness and global demand uncertainty temper sentiment.
sectors.implications: Junior miners benefit from discovery headlines but face funding risk (Bathla collapse, ASIC referral). Majors (BHP.AX, RIO.AX) supported by copper/gold exploration pipeline but pressured by global growth fears.

sectors.trend: RBA hiking into rising unemployment creates margin pressure vs credit loss risk. Bond yield spike pressures equity valuations. Intergenerational Report flags fiscal tightening ahead.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX face squeezed net interest margins if RBA hikes further while credit losses rise. Defensive dividend appeal intact but upside limited.

sectors.trend: Fuel price fears as global buffers dry up; Trump diesel export ban threatens supply. Energy cost political dispute (Labor vs Coalition) adds policy uncertainty. Nuclear energy debate resurfaces.
sectors.implications: Woodside (WDS.AX), Santos (STO.AX) benefit from higher energy prices but face policy risk. Solar/tech (ClearVue) gains attention. Energy 'hysteria' suggests overreaction risk.

sectors.trend: Renter stress, Jetstar industrial action, and Ozempic-driven demand shifts pressure consumer names. McDonald's adapting to weight-loss drug boom.
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WOL.AX face margin pressure from input costs and wage disputes. CSL.AX (healthcare) benefits from obesity drug pipeline (Viking Therapeutics data).

sectors.trend: Rising listings and falling demand driving prices lower. Chinese property recovery uncertain. RBA hikes further suppress affordability.
sectors.implications: REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX) face occupancy and yield pressure. Property developers (SRG.AX, CGP.AX) under stress. Bathla collapse signals construction sector fragility.

sectors.trend: $16b Aussie tech firm faces China-link controversy. Nine leadership change. AI workplace adoption and data breach concerns. US tech (Microsoft, AMD, Micron) showing strength.
sectors.implications: ASX tech names face geopolitical risk from China exposure. Media (NEG.AX) in flux. Global AI/semiconductor strength (NVDA, AMD) provides indirect sentiment support.

key_themes: Stagflation risk: RBA hiking into 5-year high unemployment
AUD/USD weakness driven by US economic outperformance
Trump trade policy (diesel ban, market cracks) as external shock
Mining exploration pipeline (copper, gold, rare earths) remains robust
Fiscal sustainability: Intergenerational Report flags tax reform need
Consumer stress: renters, industrial action, fuel costs

risk_assessment.risk_factor: RBA rate hike into rising unemployment (stagflation)
risk_assessment.mitigation: Overweight quality dividend payers; reduce leverage; hedge with gold (GOLD.AX, NVL.AX)
Export-oriented miners (BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX) benefit; hedge AUD exposure in portfolios

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Trump diesel export ban / energy supply disruption
risk_assessment.mitigation: Monitor WDS.AX, STO.AX; consider energy infrastructure plays; diversify away from fuel-dependent sectors

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Property market correction and construction sector fragility
risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce REIT and developer exposure; monitor GPW.AX, SRG.AX; Bathla/ASIC cases signal broader risk
Shorten duration in fixed income; favour short-duration equities; monitor ^AORD vs ^AXJO
Monitor QAN.AX; reduce consumer discretionary exposure; favour staples (WES.AX)

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold and copper miners on exploration momentum and AUD weakness
opportunities.rationale: Multiple high-grade discoveries (Auric, Forrestania, Sarytogan, Rio2) plus AUD depreciation boosts AUD-denominated earnings

opportunities.recommendation: Add energy producers on fuel supply fears and Trump diesel ban
opportunities.rationale: Global buffer depletion and export restrictions support upstream energy pricing; WDS/STO benefit

opportunities.recommendation: Selective healthcare/obesity drug exposure via CSL
opportunities.rationale: Viking Therapeutics obesity data positive; CSL.AX benefits from global GLP-1 pipeline expansion

defensive_moves.rationale: Rising listings, falling demand, Bathla collapse, and RBA hikes create downside risk for property sector

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hedge equity portfolio with quality bonds and gold
defensive_moves.rationale: Bond yield spike and stagflation risk favour fixed income and gold as diversifiers

defensive_moves.recommendation: Trim consumer discretionary and transport names amid industrial action
defensive_moves.rationale: Jetstar dispute and renter stress signal consumer spending weakness

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain under pressure from RBA hike, bond yield spike, and AUD weakness. Stagflation narrative dominates. Expect volatility in ^AXJO and ^AORD. Mining and energy outperform; property, consumer, and banks lag. 1-3 month outlook: cautious, range-bound with downside risk.
market_outlook.long_term: 6-12 month outlook stabilises if RBA pauses and unemployment peaks. Mining exploration pipeline (copper, gold, rare earths) supports structural demand. Tax reform from Intergenerational Report may create fiscal headwinds. Property correction likely to continue. AUD stabilises if US growth moderates.
